answer: Each identity claims one bridge footing on a knoll terrace, locks a 70-credit bond and files a signed sinking reading. The auditor recomputes it from the footing load table and terrace survey; out-of-range, missing, or reused-serial readings burn the bond. The first filing costs 28 credits, the k-th costs 28+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,022; 1,000 fakes pay 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-footing ring fails: a rented reading carries its owner's key, so the same serial under a second key triggers a double burn. An honest agent pays 28 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
